title: Thunkable vs Emergent
summary: Looking for an Emergent alternative? Thunkable pairs AI with a visual editor, so you can fix and publish a native iOS and Android app yourself, without waiting on another agent run.
body_markdown:
Emergent uses AI agents to design, code and deploy full-stack web and mobile apps, and you own the code. For teams that want generated code they can hand to developers, that's a real draw.


But every AI builder hits the same moment: the app is almost right, and the agent can't get it the rest of the way. What you can do next is the real difference between the Emergent app builder and Thunkable.


**Quick verdict:** Thunkable is an AI mobile app builder with a visual editor for native iOS and Android apps. To build and fix a native app yourself, without reading code, it's the better fit. Emergent suits teams that want to own generated code and have developers to extend it.


‍


## **Why founders choose Thunkable to finish their app**


- **You can always finish it.** When the AI gets close, open the visual editor and fix screens and logic yourself.
- **Plan before you build.** Discuss Mode helps you plan changes and troubleshoot before anything is built.
- **Roll back anytime.** Version History lets you undo a change that didn't work.
- **Native and publish-ready.** 25+ device features and a built-in path to the App Store and Google Play.
- **A decade of mobile behind the AI.** Launched in 2016, with more than 5 million creators.


*"We're talking five weeks for somebody that's never written a mobile app or programmed a mobile app in his life." (Ronnie Sherard, founder, Amazing Aurora)*


‍

## **What Emergent is, and where it shines**


Emergent pitches full-stack web and mobile apps built by AI agents, with paid plans starting at about $17 to $20 a month. It builds mobile apps with Expo, whose cloud service can submit to both the App Store and Google Play.


It shines when code ownership matters. If you have developers ready to take the generated code and extend it, Emergent is worth a look.


‍


## **Does the Emergent app builder make native mobile apps?**


Both tools can produce native mobile apps. Emergent generates native mobile code through Expo. Thunkable builds native iOS and Android apps from the first prompt, with 25+ native device features, including camera, barcode scanning, GPS and maps, push notifications, biometrics, NFC and Bluetooth.


‍


## **What happens when Emergent's AI gets stuck?**


This is where the two tools part ways.


On Emergent, each agent run spends credits, and Emergent's help center says those credits also pay for hosting and don't roll over. When the agent can't fix something, the next step is another run or reading the code yourself.


On Thunkable, you're never stuck waiting on another run to fix a button. When the AI gets close:


- **Use Discuss Mode** to troubleshoot and plan the fix before you ask for another change.
- **Open the visual editor** and tweak screens and logic directly.
- **Edit the code** if you want to go deeper.
- **Roll back** with Version History if a change doesn't work.


You stay in control of the final fixes.


‍


## **How do you publish an Emergent or Thunkable app?**


Emergent can submit to both stores through Expo's cloud service. Thunkable publishes to the App Store, Google Play and the web in a few clicks, from the same place you build, with publishing guides and AI checklists to help you through review.


‍


## **Emergent vs Thunkable: predictability**


Emergent's credits pay for both building and hosting, so a live app keeps drawing from the balance every month, and unused monthly credits don't roll over, according to Emergent's help center. Plans run from $20/mo on Standard to $200/mo on Pro, according to Emergent's pricing page.


On Thunkable, AI tokens go to building: a Build prompt uses about 250 tokens and a Discuss Mode prompt 100, according to Thunkable's docs. Your published apps stay available to your users as long as your paid plan is active, according to Thunkable's pricing page.


**Where Thunkable comes out ahead:** On Emergent, credits pay for both building and hosting, and a stuck build means another run. On Thunkable, you open the visual editor and fix the screen or the logic yourself, without waiting on the AI.


‍


## **Switching from Emergent to Thunkable**


If you're stuck mid-build or watching hosting credits drain, here's how to move:


1. **Export what you have.** Emergent lets you export your code, so keep a copy before you leave.
2. **Describe the app to Thunkable AI.** List your screens and flows as the brief.
3. **Finish it yourself.** Use the visual editor for the last fixes instead of another agent run.
4. **Publish to both stores** with publishing guides and AI checklists.

## **FAQ**


- ‍ **Is Thunkable a good Emergent alternative?** Yes, if you want to finish and publish a native app yourself. The visual editor means you're never stuck waiting on another agent run. **‍**
- **Does Emergent build mobile apps?** Yes. It builds mobile apps with Expo, and Expo's cloud service can submit to both stores. **‍**
- **What happens on Thunkable when the AI can't fix something?** You can fix it yourself in the visual editor, plan the change in Discuss Mode, or edit code directly. **‍**
- **Do I need to read code to use Thunkable?** No. Code editing is available, but you can build and fix your app with AI and the visual editor.


**When the AI gets close, finish it yourself.** Thunkable's visual editor lets you tweak screens and logic directly, so you're never stuck mid-build.
